assumptions: The R-419 conditional law is positive and normalized and the projected conductance is symmetric and nonnegative.
The R-421 Lyapunov vector and tail threshold are reused without retuning per row.
The sqrt(pi) transform identifies weighted L2 norm with Euclidean norm and preserves the finite Dirichlet form.
The core basis is block-mean-zero, so the two-dimensional block-constant coarse sector is excluded from the residual audit.
The spectral norm and restricted eigenvalues are computed from the declared finite matrices and never rounded upward in the reserve test.
The Lean proof is a scalar algebraic cross-check, not a formalization of the full numerical matrix lane.
boundary: R-422 closes only the finite scalar reserve inequality and its bounded Q3 diagnostic. It does not close the Q3LOCK common-alpha or broken-sector coercivity parents, and negative finite reserve rows are not a theorem of physical gaplessness.
evidence_level: T0 / exact finite two-block form inequality plus executed Q3-row reserve diagnostic; no uniform theorem or physical conclusion
missing_assumptions: A cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform lower bound for the tail Hardy floor and core restricted form on one Hamiltonian common core.
A uniform upper bound on the core-tail cross block or an analytic boundary-capacity estimate that makes lambda_minus positive.
A compatible treatment of the two-dimensional block-mean coarse sector and its Schur complement.
Two-sided form-norm control of actual R-399 histories and a common split-limit map.
Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS/GNS identification and a sectorwise coercive estimate.
non_claims: No cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform reserve.
No global Poincare or full Schur theorem for arbitrary observables.
No control of the block-constant coarse sector.
No common Hamiltonian core or split-limit dynamics.
No OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction or sectorwise spectral gap.
No continuum, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.
